amends: l1_background_level_perframe_vs_onstack — how the CONFIRMED-AS-EQUIVALENT branch must be written. It changes no arm, no knob and no threshold; the pre-registered 0.90 line stays binding.
raised_by: the parallel audit session, after its own mechanism had been falsified; re-derived here from this session's records before adoption, and it lands wider than the note claimed (0.79-1.36x rather than 0.98-1.26x)
written_when: before arm A produced a single reading — the arm was still building. SE_A is therefore ASSUMED equal to SE_B here; the combined SE is recomputed from arm A's own measured SE when it lands.
the_two_branches_are_not_equally_powered: on the powered sets the REFUTATION branch is a real test and the EQUIVALENCE branch is close to a tautology, and they must not be reported in the same voice.
refutation_branch_is_reachable: falsifier A fires below 0.90 - 2*SE: set-01 at retained < 0.788/0.758/0.780 (arm A destroying 21/24/22% of the relation), set-02 at < 0.755/0.764/0.773 (24/24/23%). That is arm A having to beat a single sky-plane's entire budget by about 2x — precisely what the pre-registered mechanism says a SUM of planes fitted in SENSOR coordinates to drifting frames might do. Reachable, so the branch is a test.
equivalence_branch_is_bounded_by_the_eff: the catalogue plane bound maps DIRECTLY onto the retained scale — removing the plane component of the predictor leaves a slope ratio of about 1 - R2_plane(x) — which is where the 0.90 line came from in the first place (set-01's bound is 10.0%, floor 0.900). So an on-stack plane can move retained by AT MOST 0.100 on set-01, 0.075 on set-02, 0.149 on set-03, 0.064 on the union. Against that, the 1-SE equivalence window is 0.0789/0.1002/0.0845 on set-01 and 0.1023/0.0962/0.0901 on set-02 — window/bound = 0.79x / 1.00x / 0.85x and 1.36x / 1.28x / 1.20x. THE WINDOW AND THE WHOLE MEASURABLE EFFECT ARE THE SAME SIZE.
how_the_equivalence_result_must_be_writt: as 'the arms agree to within about 8-10 points of retained, which is the size of the entire budget an on-stack plane has', NEVER as a bare 'the arms are equivalent'. An equivalence finding here cannot separate 'both arms are gentle on the starlight' from 'the instrument cannot see an on-stack plane's effect at all', because those two predict the same measurement. Same shape as the per-group-flat result whose composed-level difference was zero BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by luck: a null is only a result when the instrument could have seen the effect.
the_0_90_line_is_set_01s_bound_applied_u: stated because it is not neutral across surfaces. The line's own rationale is 'more than the whole degree-1 sky-plane budget', and that budget is surface-specific: 1 - bound gives 0.900 on set-01 (exact), 0.925 on set-02, 0.851 on set-03, 0.936 on the union. It stays the binding number here (an acceptance measure does not move without user ratification, and this would be tightening it by argument). Both lines are reported per surface.
and_the_direction_is_NOT_the_same_everyw: do not carry '0.90 is conservative'. It is conservative on set-02 (0.925) and the union (0.936) — harder to fire than the rationale implies — and ANTI-CONSERVATIVE on set-03, whose own line is 0.851: there, 0.90 would fire on damage that set-03's own catalogue bound says a single plane could legitimately have done. Moot in practice, since set-03's retained_se is 0.334 and falsifier A cannot fire there at all, but the general statement would be wrong.
falsifier_A_IS_the_directional_hypothesi: worth stating in the verdict rather than leaving as arithmetic. Because the expected retained for a perfect on-stack plane is exactly the single-plane budget, `retained_A < 0.90` is not a threshold sitting beside the hypothesis — it IS the hypothesis, stated as a measurement: does the per-frame step remove more than any one sky-plane could have? The pre-registration's prose treats the line and the mechanism as two things; they are one, and the test is better-posed than its own wording knew.
how_exact_the_mapping_is_and_where_it_st:
EXACT only for an idealised image that is starlight alone: with floor = a*x, subtracting the best-fit plane leaves a*x_perp and regressing on x returns a*var(x_perp)/var(x) = a*(1 - R2_plane). ANY confound correlated with the predictor breaks it, and PLANARITY IS IRRELEVANT to that — which is the opposite of what it first looks like. Seeded fixture, 140 cells, 1 - R2_plane(x) = 0.6201, true starlight coefficient a = 3.0:
  confound                 numerator   denominator   retained(instrument)
  none                        1.8604        3.0000                 0.6201
  purely planar, small        1.8604        2.7791                 0.6694
  purely planar, huge         1.8604       -7.2081                -0.2581
  quadratic                   1.8579        3.0188                 0.6154
  on x's own non-plane part   0.9302        2.0698                 0.4494
The NUMERATOR is untouched by a purely planar confound of any amplitude — a plane fit removes it entirely — so a ratio taken against the TRUE starlight slope stays exact at 0.6201 in all three planar rows. But the instrument does not have the true slope and never can: `retained` is (ctrl_slope + delta_slope)/ctrl_slope, so it divides by the CONTROL'S MEASURED slope, and that denominator moves with any correlated confound, planar or not.
and_this_is_the_mechanism_behind_retaine: the same fixture reproduces the pre-registration's own stated confound quantitatively. An ANTI-correlated instrumental term depresses the denominator (3.0000 -> 2.7791 -> -7.2081 as its amplitude grows) while leaving the numerator alone, so the ratio RISES — which is exactly 'the open sky x V residual is anti-correlated with the starlight and biases the raw slope low, so removing any low-order surface raises it'. It is not a separate caveat sitting beside the bound; it is the same arithmetic seen from the denominator. On these products the control's Red slope is 9.96 against arm B's 16.29, and that depressed denominator is what puts retained at 1.636 rather than below 0.90.
under_powered_surfaces_for_completeness: set-03 window/bound 3.17x/2.82x/1.33x, union 6.30x/6.93x/3.83x. On the union the equivalence window is up to seven times the entire effect, which is the quantitative form of 'this surface cannot separate anything'.
what_would_close_it: not more precision on this instrument — the bound is a property of the OPERATOR (a plane's reach over this predictor), not of the measurement. Separating the two arms at the scale of a plane's own budget needs either a field where a plane can absorb more of the starlight (the bound is per-field and the instrument prints it every run), or a criterion other than starlight preservation. Stated so the next session does not re-run this expecting a sharper answer.
